stages.name: Phishing and AitM Token Theft
observables: fake login pages capturing usernames and passwords

stages.name: Brute Force and Password Spraying
observables: testing common passwords (e.g., Password01) across multiple accounts
credential stuffing using data from previous breach dumps

stages.name: Infostealer Credential Harvesting
observables: theft of browser cookies and session tokens
harvesting of autofill data from endpoints
infostealer execution disguised as fake downloads or ads

stages.name: Local Credential Dumping
observables: Use of Mimikatz to extract password hashes
copying SAM, SECURITY, and SYSTEM Registry hives to capture hashes

stages.name: Abuse of Valid Accounts for Lateral Movement
observables: impossible travel (logins from two distant locations in a short timeframe)
use of legitimate employee credentials to reach internal applications

stages.name: Impact and Ransomware Encryption
observables: business email compromise involving fraudulent wire transfers

scenario.summary: Threat actors use phishing, adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) attacks, and infostealers to obtain valid credentials and session tokens. These stolen identities fuel lateral movement, privilege escalation, and credential dumping to achieve high-impact outcomes like business email compromise and ransomware.

meta.hypothesis: An adversary is leveraging stolen credentials or brute-force techniques to bypass identity controls, visible through anomalous authentication patterns and DNS traffic to proxy or AitM infrastructure.

hunt.name: Identity Plane Authentication and Account Abuse
hunt.description: This hunt examines the identity plane for evidence of credential abuse across both on-premises and cloud resources. It begins by scoping the estate to systems hosting Active Directory or identity services to focus on the core authentication infrastructure. The hunt then gathers evidence from three independent telemetry streams: large-scale password spraying attempts (authentication failures), successful logins from rare or new source IPs per user targeting specific resources, and DNS resolutions to known proxy and AitM (Adversary-in-the-Middle) frameworks. An agent then weighs these three streams to identify high-confidence account compromises and lateral movement.

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%active directory%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%domain services%')
config.description: Identify systems hosting Active Directory or identity services where credential dumping and authentication logs are most critical.
config.expected_signal: A list of hostnames representing the identity-critical estate. Silence suggests no systems are explicitly identified as domain controllers in the inventory.

primitive_config.label: Scope to Identity Assets
primitive_config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%active directory%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%domain services%')
primitive_config.expected: A list of hostnames representing the identity-critical estate. Silence suggests no systems are explicitly identified as domain controllers in the inventory.

config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, actor_user_domain, COUNT(DISTINCT actor_user_name) AS unique_accounts, COUNT(*) AS failure_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE activity_id = 5 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || dst_endpoint_name || ',') > 0) GROUP BY src_endpoint_ip, actor_user_domain HAVING unique_accounts >= {{spray_threshold}} ORDER BY unique_accounts DESC
config.description: Detect source IPs attempting to authenticate against multiple accounts, signaling automated spraying or credential stuffing.
config.expected_signal: IPs targeting more than the threshold of accounts across a domain or specific scoped host. Silence proves an absence of large-scale automated spraying against the scoped systems.

primitive_config.label: Password Spraying Attempts
primitive_config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, actor_user_domain, COUNT(DISTINCT actor_user_name) AS unique_accounts, COUNT(*) AS failure_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE activity_id = 5 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || dst_endpoint_name || ',') > 0) GROUP BY src_endpoint_ip, actor_user_domain HAVING unique_accounts >= {{spray_threshold}} ORDER BY unique_accounts DESC
primitive_config.expected: IPs targeting more than the threshold of accounts across a domain or specific scoped host. Silence proves an absence of large-scale automated spraying against the scoped systems.

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_name, mfa, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 1 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || dst_endpoint_name || ',') > 0) GROUP BY actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_name
config.description: Identify successful logins from source IPs that are uncommon for a specific user and destination, potentially indicating session or account takeover.
config.expected_signal: A list of successful authentications. Prevalence will highlight rare combinations of IP and target resource per user.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, query_hostname, COUNT(*) AS lookup_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE activity_id = 1 AND (instr(',' || '{{proxy_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, process_name, query_hostname
config.description: Corroborate anomalous logins with DNS resolutions to proxy or AitM infrastructure frequently used to disguise origin or intercept tokens.
config.expected_signal: Hosts resolving domains like torproject.org or ngrok.io in the same window as anomalous logins. Silence indicates no visible proxy traffic via DNS.

config.objective: Identify compromised accounts by correlating brute-force IPs with subsequent successful logins and identifying any accompanying proxy infrastructure traffic on the same hosts.
config.description: Determine if any user accounts have been successfully compromised based on the coincidence of spray attempts, rare successful logins, and proxy infrastructure usage.
config.expected_signal: A per-host/user verdict identifying malicious session or account takeover.
config.success_criteria: A per-user verdict (malicious | suspicious | benign) citing source IPs, target resources, MFA usage, and any correlated proxy DNS traffic.

config.question: the triage verdict is malicious for at least one account, indicating high-confidence credential abuse
config.condition: the triage verdict is malicious for at least one account, indicating high-confidence credential abuse
config.description: Direct the hunt to containment if an account compromise is confirmed.
Contain the impact by isolating the host where abuse was detected and revoking the compromised user's identity sessions.
config.instructions: Isolate the compromised endpoint cited in the triage verdict. Revoke all active sessions for the compromised user account and reset their password immediately.

config.description: Review findings to confirm the compromise scope and record tuning notes for the spraying threshold.
config.instructions: Audit the cited account's recent activity for lateral movement or data access. Determine if MFA was bypassed or legitimately approved. Record if the spraying threshold produced excessive noise from legitimate services.

config.description: Finalize the hunt and document the absence of credential abuse.
config.instructions: Document that no anomalous authentication spikes or proxy-correlated logins were observed for the period. Archive findings.
